label: Край
description: A 10-sentence usage card for край (edge; region).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative predicate. 'Край' is the masculine nominative predicate noun meaning native region. 'Родной' is the agreeing masculine adjective, a warm way to name one's homeland.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Край' is the accusative direct object of 'люблю'; as an inanimate masculine noun its accusative matches the nominative. 'Свой' agrees in masculine gender.
Strategic focus: Accusative of direction. 'Край' is the accusative goal after 'на', meaning onto the edge. 'Стола' is the genitive showing whose edge, a concrete spatial line.
Strategic focus: Genitive with 'до'. 'Края' is genitive after 'до', marking the limit reached. 'Леса' is a second genitive showing whose edge, a clean motion-to pattern.
Strategic focus: Locative prepositional in -у. 'Край' takes the special locative ending 'краю' after 'на' to mean right at the edge. 'На самом' intensifies the precarious position.
Strategic focus: Locative prepositional in -у. 'Краю' is the special -у locative after 'на', meaning on the outskirts. 'Города' is the genitive showing whose edge.
Strategic focus: Instrumental object. 'Краем' is the instrumental case required by 'любуются', the region being admired. 'Нашим' agrees in the masculine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional with 'в'. 'Крае' is the standard prepositional form after 'в' describing where things are. 'Много лесов' uses the genitive plural after a quantity word.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Края' is the nominative plural of 'край', the subject. 'Эти' agrees in the plural and 'красивы' is the short adjective praising the region.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural with 'из'. 'Краёв' is the genitive plural after 'из', marking origin. 'Далёких' agrees in the genitive plural, a poetic way to say from faraway lands.
